g.text: Sync Mechanisms
BroadcastChannel API (Modern)
const ch = new BroadcastChannel('app_state')
ch.postMessage({type:'CART_UPDATE', payload})
ch.onmessage = (e) => dispatch(e.data)
Same origin only. Does NOT persist.
Best: low latency, clean API, no storage pollution
localStorage + storage Event (Compat)
Tab A: localStorage.setItem('cart', JSON.stringify(data))
Tab B: window.addEventListener('storage', handler)
Fires only in OTHER tabs (not emitting tab)
Fallback for BroadcastChannel (IE/older). Persists across sessions.
SharedWorker (Advanced)
Single worker shared across all tabs of origin
Tabs connect to worker via port — worker routes messages
Can hold shared state centrally (auth, cart)
Best for complex coordination. Overkill for simple sync.
Use Cases & Patterns
Critical Sync Scenarios
Auth state: login/logout propagates to all tabs immediately
Shopping cart: add item in Tab A → Tab B cart updates
Session timeout: timer fires → all tabs log out together
Settings: user changes theme → all tabs apply immediately
Notifications: new notification badge updates all tabs
Lock: prevent concurrent editing (tab A has lock, Tab B shows warning)
Leader election: one tab drives polling/WebSocket, others follow
Rule: sync security state (auth) eagerly; sync UX state lazily
Conflict & Race Conditions
Two tabs write simultaneously: last-write-wins (LWW by timestamp)
Message ordering: BroadcastChannel is ordered per sender, not global
Idempotent handlers: receiving same message twice should be safe
Include version/sequence in messages to detect stale updates
Don't sync derived state — sync source facts, recompute locally
Circular echo: don't re-broadcast messages received from other tabs
Leader Election Pattern
Tabs compete to be leader (hold WebSocket, timer, polling)
Leader heartbeats via BroadcastChannel. On leader close, new election runs.
Libraries: broadcast-channel, tab-master. Reduces duplicate server connections.

svg.text: Always sync: auth logout (security). Consider sync: cart, theme, notifications.
Zustand: built-in cross-tab sync via persist + storage event listener.
